definition: Neural cryptography is a branch of cryptography dedicated to analyzing the application of stochastic algorithms, especially artificial neural network algorithms, for use in encryption and cryptanalysis.
details: Neural cryptography is a branch of cryptography dedicated to analyzing the application of stochastic algorithms, especially artificial neural network algorithms, for use in encryption and cryptanalysis.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — Neural cryptography — is what makes everything else possible.
